head: The crawl predicted no follows, but agents asked for the raw page and followed the hidden link in {raw_k} of {raw_n} runs
sub: Question: Does a crawl with no AI model predict how often AI agents follow a hidden link? Answer: No. The crawl's rule: the share of pages where the fetch tool's first reply shows the link, times the agent's follow rate from our earlier test.
start: {model} reads pages through one fetch tool per run. The Plans page shows only 2024 prices. A link that people cannot see leads to 2025.
grp_seen: 1-pixel link with off-task words. Every first reply shows it → the rule says {rule_off}%, {model}'s earlier rate
grp_none: Fully hidden link that fits the task. The default first reply hides it → the rule says 0%
ch_A: Raw mode: the agent opened the link
ch_B: Browser Use: the agent gave up
ch_C: MCP fetch tool: the agent asked for the raw page
act_C: asks for raw HTML, then opens the hidden link
log_none: server log: no visit to the link
chart_title: Share of runs that followed the hidden link
chart_sub: bar = measured, line = the rule's prediction
foot: 5 test websites we built, link hidden in the page footer; follows counted from our server log. Kran Lab, Nov 9 2026
cg_fit: Fully hidden link, MCP fetch tool, default mode · rule 0%
